revision_notes: Confirmed: Comoros has no standardised postal/address code system. revision_notes: Confirmed: a Bureau du Cadastre exists under the Direction Générale des Impôts (dgi.gouv.km) but cadastral surveying (levée topographique, plan croquis) remains a manual, paper-based procedure taking 104-158 days (eRegulations Comores, accessed 2026). A 2024/2025 GIS pilot using 2018 orthophotos covers only a small Moroni test zone, not a national digital cadastral database. No evidence of a fully digitised national cadastre. Value Code 1 (No) is supported; code unchanged.

Definition: Does the government maintain a digital population register?
Comments: No credible evidence found for digital population register after searching government sites, World Bank ID4D (no data), ANADEN strategy, e-gov portal, general web/academic searches.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original 'No' is outdated. As of March 2026, the government (Ministry of Interior, with UNICEF/French Embassy support via the AMECC programme) validated preparatory studies for full computerisation of the civil/population registry, underpinned by a 27 July 2023 law mandating digitised data processing and introducing a unique Personal Identification Number (NIP) intended to centralise citizen records; UNICEF's 2024 country report confirms a validated 2024-2028 modernisation strategic plan with initial 2025 budget allocation (USD429,000 of an estimated USD8.7m). However, local reporting explicitly describes the current system as 'still largely manual', so no operational digital register exists yet — this is a funded, legally-mandated plan at the preparatory-study stage, not yet under technical development. Revised to 2 (Planned). Note: sources describe the civil registration (CRVS) reform rather than a distinct population register; flagged for human review given possible overlap between the two variables.
